Comprehensive review — Mermaid Roshan and the Hidden Rainbow

Reviewed 30 September 2026. Edition: v27_correct_door, source commit f857a65e95d5d7846af19f27046735a74cba4ec4. This is an editorial and visual review, not a revised edition. No book art, manuscript, font, layout code or PDF has been changed.

The book has a strong emotional spine: Roshan makes a place for everyone by helping them. A focused continuity, action and page-turn pass is the most useful next step. The bath payoff, Rumi's hug, messy art-table composition, group scrub and sleeping ensemble are worth protecting. The current weaknesses are concentrated enough to fix without losing those gains.

Scope, evidence and numbering

All 34 current PDF pages were rendered with Poppler at 144 dpi and inspected individually. All 34 original-book pages were rendered at 100 dpi and inspected on six contact sheets, with selected enlarged reference pages also consulted. The current source manifest, page-layer provenance, manuscript, design language, prior correction evidence and supplied editorial feedback were cross-checked. The original PDF was actually inspected; the older pasted critique explicitly lacked that comparison.

S1–S32 means story pages. PDF page = story page + 1. Front cover is PDF1; rear cover is PDF34. The book correctly contains 32 story pages plus two covers. There is no recommendation to cut two pages merely because the review PDF has 34.

Priorities: P1 = resolve before a final editorial/print proof; P2 = targeted refinement; P3 = preserve and verify. A priority is not a judgment that an entire page should be regenerated. Proposed copy below is an editing option, not an approved replacement; conditional wording must wait for matching source art.

The review distinguishes observed visual problems, editorial preferences and source questions. It does not claim child testing, physical print acceptance, complete numeric border-mask certification or a new game/cinematic audit pass.

The corrections that matter most

  1. Make the rescue action unmistakable, S16–18. The dusty room changes into a bright clean playroom without an intervening event. On S18 the brush crosses Eagle's wing beside his face, while the bunnies are already next to him. Align the location and show one bunny released and the other being gently moved. Preserve exactly two bunnies and the existing game event.
  2. Give the final reflection its recipient, S31. “Your rainbow” currently accompanies Daddy and Roshan alone; Daddy has a rainbow tail. Include restored Grand Puff and name him in the line.
  3. Show the cleaning cause as well as the result, S6 and S11–13. The sink page lacks a wiping actor, the waterfall lacks a clear action image, and the cup against the seahorse's mouth can read as being offered rather than removed. Source search and local contact edits come before new generation.
  4. Check castle geography, S3 versus S24. S3 contains theatrical masks/book/pot door symbols; S24 now uses the correct shell-door approach and completed-room route. The mismatch is real, but whether these are intentionally different spaces requires a canonical source check. Do not blindly replace either room.
  5. Keep compassion clear through the Puff action, S25–27. Roshan promises help, then Puff becomes dizzy while bunnies cheer and eat popcorn. Preserve the requested action and spectators; use gaze, concern and a short reassuring line to make the cheering about help, not suffering.
  6. Repair the four stretched ceiling extensions, S27–30. Their vertical source density is only approximately 116–138 ppi and their proportions differ from the retained scenes. Repair the extensions while protecting the accepted scrub, concealment, leap and landing.
  7. Make page turns do narrative work. In a conventional dummy with S1 on the right, S24/S25 and S28/S29 share spreads: both reveals are visible alongside their setups. Validate physical pagination before moving pages.
  8. Finish optical text placement and the apology conversation. Text boxes are mechanically within trim, but some outlined captions compete with detailed architecture/props. S19 has proper ellipses now; their size and pointed tails still overwhelm the small speakers.

What the first book teaches this edition

The reference's design language is a rhythm, not merely a dotted border. It uses quieter pale aqua stationery, small contextual lower objects, varied sizes of genuinely isolated figures and scenes that sometimes occupy the whole page. The small recurring actions reward another reading without competing with the main event.

The current book has 22 full-art and 10 cutout story pages. In the original's 32 interior pages, the visual count is 13 full-art and 19 framed/cutout pages. These are descriptive counts, not a target ratio. The current uninterrupted full-art run from S11 through S18 particularly reduces contrast between water cleanup, Rumi's thanks and the next rescue.

Consider converting S13's connected fountain action and S15's hug into genuine silhouette compositions, if complete source contours support them. This would give 20 full-art and 12 cutout story pages before any pagination experiment. Do not use irregular scenic blobs as a substitute. Keep the rainbow, emergence, rescue, POP and nap large.

Useful original-book precedents include original PDF4's scale contrast, PDF13's alternating figure/text arrangement, PDF16's multiple cooking actions, PDF21's action/result composition and PDF28's sleeping Eagle at the bottom. Borrow the compositional logic, not a rigid grid or unrelated legacy characters. Original PDF11 identifies Lamb-a by name.

Keep the blue base, but make its wash and dotted perimeter quieter: the current saturated cloudy blue, dark perimeter and outlined banks sometimes feel like a game interface. Judge this at print size before applying a global adjustment. Quiet space is purposeful; empty space becomes a problem when the narrated action is absent. Do not fill every gap with another prop, bunny or bubble.

A coherent border and cutout art direction

Each reduced page should have one main foreground action and one small contextual echo below. The two low blue banks and central gap are stable; the activity, emphasis and figure count vary. Zero bunnies can be right. One to three are allowed where they add meaning. Full-art pages have no stationery.

Use the strong existing S21 messy-art border as a quality anchor. S7's duck/towel, S10's actual rubbish, S20's toy play, S25's cowering/shell grouping and S26's couch/popcorn already have clear jobs. They need selective polish, not replacement with a new batch of generic cleaning symbols. S31's cooperative puzzle play is an appropriate quiet echo of friendship.

Ground objects with the actual bank shape, perspective, local contact and restrained shadow. Never claim a precise hidden-10% occlusion or exact alpha extraction for generated flattened pixels when that was not measured. Retain the established decorative size/zone rules and no-duplicate-prop rule. S19's speaking bunnies are narrative actors, covered by its existing scoped exception; compose them with Eagle rather than shrinking them to decorative stamps.

Avoid smudges as ornaments, repeated identical brushes, pools of generic suds, perfectly identical bunny poses and clean decorative objects on rubbish pages. Preserve supplied contours, natural holes and character proportions. A complete sink, book or table can have a rectangular physical outline; a rectangle of surrounding room cannot.

Identity and illustration continuity

Build a small internal identity board from approved sources before touching outliers. Roshan's brown hair/rainbow placement, crown, purple clothing, eyes, tail and head/body proportions should remain recognizable through every pose. S20/S21 show a noticeable proportion/style transition; S26/S27 should also be checked for the jump to a much smaller chibi Roshan. Variation in pose is welcome; a different apparent child is not.

Baby Eagle's painted rescue version and flatter S19/S20 cutouts need a side-by-side eye, beak, feather, wing and gray-foot check. The two later poses are already different—do not repeat the obsolete duplicate-image complaint. For the bunnies, use the original lavender cloud/curl-ear/pearl-hand reference rather than an earlier generated derivative as the design authority.

Rumi should read as the same adult mermaid in the pool, emergence, hug, group help and cover. Check the relative apparent-age/eye-shape changes, especially between her submerged and cover treatments. Her hundreds of years belong to her residence in the castle, not a centuries-long entrapment.

Grand Puff is one individual before and after restoration. Preserve identifying contours through the dusty, bubbly, airborne and landed poses. Do not replace his accepted landing or imply that a separate creature comes out of him. Prior scoped owner commissions permit named rescue/quality/identity corrections; they are not general permission to invent new game scenes.

Story, emotional logic and pacing

The book's sequence is coherent: arrive, start small, restore the water, free Rumi, rescue Eagle, make art, help Puff, rest together. Rumi and Eagle later helping Puff gives the kindness a satisfying return. Keep that connection visually clear.

The weak middle transitions are manageable. Move from Eagle's apology/gentle play into the art room with a short invitation or visual directional cue. S21/S22/S23 can then read as sort, clean, create. On S22 the picture still contains paint residue while the text declares the table clean; align the verb tense with the actual stage.

Do not let cleaning imply that someone becomes worthy of friendship only after looking pretty. Roshan offers care while Puff is dusty and unwell. His comfort, inclusion and return to himself should carry at least as much weight as his rainbow color. The ending already offers this; preserve its warmth without adding a moralizing paragraph.

Optional 32-page turn experiment

Assume S1 starts on a right-hand page and covers are handled separately. A real dummy pairs S2/S3, S4/S5 … S30/S31, with S1 and S32 at the ends. The current browser's cover-inclusive pairs are not evidence of the final physical reading spreads. Printer, binding and front-matter choices must be settled before this convention is treated as final.

One promising experiment keeps 32 story pages: combine current S19 and S20 into one apology/forward-transition page; shift current S21–30 one page earlier; use the freed late page as a quiet view of the restored Puff receiving Roshan's reflection, using an accepted landing cutout. This places the glowing-door setup at new S23 and Puff at new S24, then bubbles at new S27 and POP at new S28. Current S31 can become the facing companion to the Puff reflection, followed by the existing nap.

Do not execute this merely to satisfy arithmetic. The resulting S30/S31 spread must read as one purposeful conversation with Puff visibly present, not two repetitive endings. Compare a paper dummy of this option with the current order. No extra new game event or full-scene invention is needed.

Language for reading together now and participation later

The current story has approximately 368 words including the five apology words, excluding covers. It is already short. Cutting it further by default would remove useful emotion and cause/effect. Prefer precise verbs, clear speakers and concrete referents over a lower word-count score.

Keep the productive repetitions: “I'll help,” “scrub, scrub,” “one little job at a time” and “little by little.” Repetition can invite Roshan to join in naturally; it need not appear mechanically on every page. “Brushes here. Paints there.” is particularly useful. Avoid the redundant gentle-play line across S19/S20, the label “playful pest” where “dust bunny” is clearer, and ambiguous “your” when the addressee is missing.

Keep a few supported richer words, such as fountain, sparkly and sprang, alongside familiar verbs. Names can remain part of shared reading. The book need not become artificially flat or all one-syllable words. Pictures should support understanding, not train a child to guess printed words from illustrations.

The editorial direction is consistent with the Institute of Education Sciences' advice on shared reading, rereading and conversation for ages 3–5: 5 Steps to Use with Young Children During Shared Book Reading Time. Later independent reading also needs sound–letter knowledge, decoding practice and connected text; this picture book is not a controlled phonics reader or a certified reading level. See Foundational Skills to Support Reading for Understanding in Kindergarten Through 3rd Grade.

Any grown-up reading suggestions belong outside the story. Do not add comprehension quizzes, “find the hidden character” instructions or a printed answer key. Let the story and the quiet visual recurrence remain rewarding on their own.

Typography and production

Sniglet is embedded and the story text is nominally 18 points. Keep it comfortably large. The extracted page-layer text boxes fall within the 7 × 5-inch trim; that mechanical check does not establish optical readability, bleed safety or gutter clearance.

Most full-art captions use navy letters with a white outline. On busy walls or art-room details that halo can look heavy while still competing with the image. Try moving the caption into naturally quiet space, then a bounded local value adjustment, then a slightly lighter outline. Do not solve this by reducing font size, covering the whole page with an opaque strip or adding new scenery.

The PDF is about 189.4 MB and uses lossless Flate image compression. The remaining softness should not be attributed to destructive JPEG compression in this PDF. Many full-page native sources are about 1484 × 1060, yielding about 212 ppi at 7 × 5 inches. That calls for actual-size print evaluation, not an automatic failure or a fictional “300 dpi” pass from upscaling.

The clearest exceptions are the stretched ceiling strips on S27–30: 116.0, 116.9, 136.7 and 137.7 effective vertical ppi, respectively. The retained lower scenes are about 239 ppi. Preserve those scenes and fix only the weak extension geometry/native detail.

This is a review PDF, not a printer-ready cover/interior package. It has no explicitly authored TrimBox/BleedBox beyond the media size. Choose the actual printer/binding specification before adding bleed, safe margins, spine, cover wrap and any publication metadata. Do not guess a universal spine width or claim a print standard is satisfied. Preserve the lossless master; a clearly labeled smaller viewing copy can be separate.

Adult-only Easter-egg plan — identity pending confirmation

The likely intended “lamma meme” is Lamb-a, the round white plush with pink cheeks and a purple egg, explicitly named in the first book. A clarification was sent; no confirmation has been received at the time this review was prepared. The placement plan is conditional on that identity. No character has been inserted or regenerated.

Reusable sources are already present: transparent Lamb-a derivative, derived from original Lamb-a design, with attribution in ASSET_LICENSES.md. Prefer the faithful transparent derivative, which omits the egg lettering. Do not turn her into a new long-necked llama or a dust bunny.

Recommend three small appearances tied to existing objects:

Current story pageHiding placeIntegration
S8 / PDF9Lower-left towel basket in the clean bathPeek from behind rolled towels; face and one ear remain recognizable.
S16 / PDF17Right-hand toy cratePartly behind an existing ball/toy; finalize only after the room-continuity repair.
S22 / PDF23Left art trolley shelfPartly hidden by existing pots; clear of the working hand and caption.

If two appearances are preferable, keep S8 and S16. Re-map by scene if pagination changes. Vary side, height and occlusion so the hiding places do not become a repeated “look in the same corner” signal.

An initial actual-size trial could use a complete asset width around 4–6% of the page, with 40–65% occluded by real foreground objects. These are proposed trial values, not measured acceptance. At 7-inch width, the whole asset would occupy about 7–11 mm; the visible face may be around 5–8 mm. Increase discreetly if she becomes an unrecognizable speck. Preserve aspect ratio and the identifying cheeks, lashes and ears.

Match local occlusion, perspective and contact. No white sticker rim, spotlight, glow, attention-directing gaze, text label, arrows, cover teaser or invitation to search. No placement during the rescues, Puff climax or final nap. She does not participate in or change the canonical action. Do not add a fourth appearance accidentally through a reused border.

Keep this map in the adult production review only. The final proof test is simple: the main story action should be noticed first, while Lamb-a remains discoverable during an unprompted later look. That behavior has not been child-tested.

Execution order and acceptance

  1. Lock the manuscript's causal chain and the physical page-turn dummy. Resolve S3 room/source authority and Lamb-a identity before dependent art edits.
  2. Correct S6, S11–13, S16–18, S22 and S31 with source reuse and bounded edits. Keep exact action/identity references beside every target.
  3. Audit identity transitions and adjust only named outliers. Preserve accepted cover H, S21 and the canonical finale.
  4. Finish the two proposed cutout conversions, border variations, S19 balloons and caption placement after the page order is settled.
  5. Repair ceiling extensions, then place the two or three subtle Lamb-a appearances. Make source hashes, local edit descriptions and placement records.
  6. Review the whole book as actual spreads, then print at actual size. Verify every face/contact, quiet caption field, cutout contour, border grounding, page edge and repeated prop. Read aloud naturally for transitions and breath.
  7. Use a quiet family reading to assess comprehension without supplying the answer: who needed help, what Roshan did and how the person felt afterward. Do not prompt for Lamb-a. This is future acceptance work, not evidence claimed by this report.

Machine checks can establish source preservation, 34-page coverage, valid links, hashes, fonts and measured placement. They cannot establish whether Roshan understands the rescue, experiences the emotional arc or discovers the Easter egg naturally.
